question: Should OpenClaw support sandboxed requesters spawning ACP sessions by running ACP inside a sandbox, by adding a host-side bridge/proxy, or by folding the behavior into a broader execution-backend placement contract?
rationale: The next step defines a sandbox-to-host trust boundary plus public config and model-facing tool semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security design.

options.title: Design A Sandbox-Aware ACP Boundary
options.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn, steer, and cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.

options.title: Require Harnesses Inside The Sandbox
options.body: Keep the current host-side ACP block and document running external harnesses inside the OpenClaw sandbox container as the supported secure path.

options.title: Defer To Execution Backends
options.body: Keep this issue open as an acceptance case while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 settles backend/profile placement and remote-worker security semantics.

recommendation.title: Design A Sandbox-Aware ACP Boundary
recommendation.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn, steer, and cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history on sessions_spawn, ACP sandbox docs, and the current ACP spawn policy surface.
